record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
record.original_question: For quantum channels T1 and T2, let chi(T) be the Holevo quantity obtained by maximizing the output entropy of an ensemble average minus the ensemble average of output entropies over input ensembles. Is chi additive under tensor products, meaning chi(T1 tensor T2) = chi(T1) + chi(T2), or is there a counterexample? Equivalently, can entanglement between signal states ever increase the classical information capacity of memoryless quantum channels beyond the single-letter Holevo expression?

evidence.quote: For each quantum channel T (in the Schrödinger picture), define χ(T) = sup H(Σi piT(ρi)) − Σi piH(T(ρi)), where the supremum is over all probability vectors p = (p1, . . . , pn), and all collections of input states {ρ1, . . ., ρn}, and H denotes the von Neumann entropy.
Show that χ(T1 ⊗ T2) = χ(T1) + χ(T2), or else give a counterexample.
This problem can also be paraphrased as “Can entanglement between signal states help to send classical information on quantum channels?”.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space and let $\mathcal{S}(\mathcal{H})$ denote the set of density operators (positive semidefinite, trace-one) on $\mathcal{H}$. A quantum channel is a completely positive trace-preserving linear map $T:\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{in}})	o\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{out}})$. For a density operator $ho$, let $H(ho)=-\mathrm{Tr}(ho\logho)$ denote the von Neumann entropy.

For a quantum channel $T$, define the Holevo quantity
$$\chi(T)\;=\;\sup\;\Big\{\,H\! ig(	extstyle\sum_i p_i\, T(ho_i) ig)\;-\;\sum_i p_i\, H(T(ho_i))\,\Big\},$$
where the supremum is over all finite probability distributions $(p_1,\dots,p_n)$ and all collections of input states $ho_1,\dots,ho_n\in\mathcal{S}(\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{in}})$.

Given two quantum channels $T_1$ and $T_2$, decide whether the identity
$$\chi(T_1\otimes T_2)\;=\;\chi(T_1)+\chi(T_2)$$
holds for every pair of channels, or exhibit channels $T_1,T_2$ for which $\chi(T_1\otimes T_2)>\chi(T_1)+\chi(T_2)$.
artifact.status_search_result: The additivity conjecture for the Holevo (classical) capacity was disproved by M. B. Hastings in 2009, who used random unitary channels in high dimension to construct counterexamples showing $\chi(T_1\otimes T_2)>\chi(T_1)+\chi(T_2)$ is possible. This also disproved the (equivalent) additivity of minimum output entropy conjecture established by Shor's equivalence theorem.

status_evidence.title: Superadditivity of communication capacity using entangled inputs
status_evidence.snippet: Hastings proves that the minimum output entropy of a quantum channel is not additive, hence the Holevo capacity is not additive.
status_evidence.claim: Hastings (2009) provided counterexamples disproving additivity of Holevo capacity.

status_evidence.title: Shor, Equivalence of additivity questions
status_evidence.snippet: Shor showed equivalence of several additivity conjectures including additivity of Holevo capacity and minimum output entropy.
status_evidence.claim: Additivity of χ is equivalent to additivity of minimum output entropy, which Hastings refuted.
